item.title: Application to change land lease conditions pending for 29 years at department
item.description: Some applications to modify land leases in Hong Kong have dragged on for years without resolution, including one that has been running for nearly three decades, the Audit Commission has found. An audit report released by the public spending watchdog on Wednesday found that the Lands Department had taken years to complete such applications. “Audit noted that a long time had been taken in completing some application cases for modification of lease conditions,” the commission said. item.title: John Lee vows full-speed push on housing, reforms ahead of Tai Po fire anniversary
item.description: Hong Kong’s leader has vowed to continue to “spare no effort” in supporting residents affected by the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire and to press ahead at full speed with housing allocation and reforms on the eve of the first anniversary of the tragedy. item.title: China promises to help Thailand and Myanmar fight Mekong basin pollution
item.description: China pledged on Wednesday to work with Thailand and Myanmar to tackle river pollution along the border between the two Southeast Asian nations. Residents in northern Thailand are facing potential water shortages and supply disruptions due to unregulated gold and rare earth mining upstream in northeastern Myanmar that has severely contaminated some tributaries of the Mekong with unsafe levels of arsenic. Bangkok asked Beijing to help close down the mines during talks between the three countries...

item.title: Consumer Council missed targets on handling complaints, product tests: audit
item.description: Hong Kong’s consumer watchdog has failed to meet performance targets for handling consumer complaints and inquiries, with shortfalls in product tests, consumer surveys and in-depth studies, an audit report has found. The Audit Commission on Wednesday released its report reviewing the operations of the Consumer Council, which is charged with resolving disputes, collecting and disseminating information, and encouraging responsible trade practices. item.title: Lawmakers call for clarity after HK$4.1 billion clawback from green projects fund
item.description: About two-thirds of a fund for green projects in Hong Kong will be brought back onto government accounts under a bill passed on Wednesday, with lawmakers calling for clarity on the city’s commitment to long-term sustainability goals. The Environment and Conservation Fund had a balance of HK$6.2 billion (US$795 million) in March, of which HK$4.1 billion will be brought back onto the government’s books.
